deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a heavily corrected prose draft of the methodological passage in Riemann's Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (1851). In the printed text this material is §20, the passage beginning 'Die Einführung der complexen Grössen in die Mathematik hat ihren Ursprung und nächsten Zweck in der Theorie einfacher ... Abhängigkeitsgesetze zwischen veränderlichen Grössen'. The draft still says 'imaginäre' where the print has 'complexe'.

Content, step by step:
(1) Imaginary quantities entered mathematics through the theory of simple dependence laws between variable quantities. Applying these laws to imaginary values reveals 'a harmony and regularity that otherwise stays hidden'.
(2) The cases treated so far cover only a small domain. Almost all reduce to dependence laws between two variables w and z where either (a) w is an algebraic function of z, i.e. F(w,z)=0 for some polynomial F, or (b) dw/dz is algebraic, i.e. w is an abelian integral such as log, arcsin, or elliptic and abelian integrals. The footnote '*' defines (a): 'd.h. wo zwischen beiden eine [algebraische] Gleichung statt findet'.
(3) Each step taken in this conception has done more than give simpler form to results obtained without imaginaries. It has also opened the way to new discoveries. The history of algebraic, circular and exponential, elliptic and Abelian functions is cited as evidence.
(4) Critique of method: all previous approaches took some particular expression of the function as their starting point. Riemann glosses such an expression as 'Bestimmungsart & Größenoperationen' and derives the general properties from it.
(5) The bottom footnote defines 'Größenoperationen = Rechnungsoperationen, bei denen die Commensurabilität oder Incommensurabilität der Größen nicht in Betracht kommt'. This anticipates the printed footnote in §20.

Other features of the page:
- Several lines written upside down (an unrelated, earlier use of the sheet) are illegible and were not reconstructed.
- The previous page deals with surfaces and boundaries (Begränzung, zusammenhängend, Begränzungstheile), i.e. the topological sections of the dissertation.
- The next page continues the argument as it appears in print: start from the 'Gestaltung' of the function (boundary and discontinuity conditions), and treat explicit expressions only as means of computing values.

The programmatic point is Riemann's well-known one: characterize functions intrinsically rather than by formulae. No implicit mathematical steps need to be supplied.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page contains no computations.
Historical claims are accurate for c. 1851. Complex methods had been applied mainly to algebraic functions and abelian integrals (Euler, Gauss, Cauchy, Abel, Jacobi).

results.what: Programmatic statement that complex values reveal hidden regularity in dependence laws; classification of the treated cases as algebraic functions and functions with algebraic derivative (abelian integrals)
results.modern_name: Motivation for complex function theory / Riemann's conceptual (intrinsic) approach to analytic functions

results.what: Critique that earlier methods define functions by a particular expression (Größenoperationen) rather than by intrinsic properties
results.modern_name: Riemann's geometric/conceptual program versus the Weierstrassian power-series approach
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 (dissertation §20); developed in the 1857 Abelian functions paper

results.what: Definition of 'Größenoperationen' as computational operations indifferent to commensurability
results.modern_name: Operations defined over a continuum (no number-theoretic or arithmetic distinctions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a well-known passage of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (§20), nearly verbatim in places. It contains no new mathematics. Its only interest is textual-genetic: the earlier wording 'imaginäre' for 'complexe', and the explicit gloss 'Bestimmungsart & Größenoperationen'.

checkable.asserts: arcsin is an example of a function whose derivative is algebraic (class (b) on the page)
log, inverse of the exponential, has algebraic (rational) derivative (class (b))
w = sqrt(1+z^2) satisfies the polynomial equation w^2 - (1+z^2) = 0, i.e. is algebraic (class (a), footnote *)

transcription_corrections: Throughout, the draft uses 'imaginären Größen'/'imaginäre Werthe'; the printed dissertation replaces these with 'complexe'.
'wurzelt [?] zuerst' is uncertain; the print reads 'hat ihren Ursprung und nächsten Zweck'. The draft wording differs and should be read from the image.
'zurückführen' (inserted top right) belongs to the phrase 'erstrecken sich fast alle auf Abhängigkeitsgesetze ... zurückführen [lassen]', matching the print 'zurückführen lassen'.
Line 3 of the third paragraph: 'wozu' is probably 'wofür', as in print: 'wofür die Geschichte ... den Beleg liefert'.
'eine {+einfache+} Gestalt' is probably 'eine einfachere Gestalt' (print: 'einfachere, abgeschlossenere Gestalt').
The inserted 'sondern auch zu neuen [?] ...' corresponds to the print 'sondern auch zu neuen Entdeckungen die Bahn gebrochen'.
Footnote *: read 'd.h. ... wo zwischen beiden eine [algebraische, struck/uncertain] Gleichung statt findet'. The struck phrase concerns the 'Wurzel einer ... algebraischen Gleichung'.
The upside-down lines in the lower middle are unrelated earlier writing on the sheet, not part of this draft.
